Country Sourdough Baker's Percentage

An everyday round or oval with a crackling crust and an irregular, open crumb. Sticky enough to want folds, then a taut skin when you shape it.

Detailed method

The times below follow the recipe this calculator opens with: 500 g flour, 75% hydration, 20% starter, 2% salt, and no added yeast. That is 375 g water, 100 g starter, and 10 g salt. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. A warm kitchen finishes sooner, and a cool kitchen needs longer. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour and the water until no dry flour remains. A dough that feels about 24°C (75°F) is a good start. If the tap water is very cold, use water that is slightly warm so the bowl does not begin chilly.
  2. Autolyse Cover the bowl and leave it for 30 minutes. Keep the starter and the salt out during this rest. The flour drinks the water, and the dough is smoother when you fold it next.
  3. Add the starter and salt Spread the starter and the salt over the dough. Pinch and fold until you cannot see streaks of either. At 75% hydration the dough is still sticky. Cover it and rest another 30 minutes.
  4. Bulk fermentation From the moment the starter goes in, keep the covered dough around 24–26°C (75–79°F) for about 4 to 4½ hours. During the first 2 hours, give it four stretch-and-folds, about 30 minutes apart. Wet your hands, lift one side, stretch it up, and fold it over the center. Turn the bowl a quarter turn and repeat until you have gone all the way around. After the last fold, leave the dough alone. It is ready when it has grown by about half, the top is domed, and a gentle shake shows bubbles just under the skin.
  5. Shape Tip the dough onto a lightly floured counter. Gently tighten it into a round and let it sit for 20 to 30 minutes. Then shape a round or an oval with a taut skin. Set it seam-side up in a floured basket, or seam-side down on a smooth cloth so it will release.
  6. Cold retard Cover the basket and refrigerate it at about 4°C (39°F) for 10 to 16 hours. The cold firms the dough, so the next day you can score it in one clean cut.
  7. Bake Heat a heavy lidded pot at 250°C (480°F) for 45 minutes. Turn the loaf onto parchment and make one cut about 1 cm deep. Lower it into the pot, cover it, and bake for 20 minutes. Take the lid off, set the oven to 230°C (450°F), and bake for another 20 to 25 minutes, until the crust is a deep brown.
  8. Cool Set the loaf on a rack. Wait at least an hour, and closer to two if you can, before you slice. The interior is still settling while it is hot, and an early cut smears instead of leaving a clean face.
